text: Keep quiet and Ill see a lawyer and do all I can And if the worst happens and them earls is too many for us theres a partnership in the grocery business ready for you when yure old enough and a home and a friend in “Yrs truly, “SILAS HOBBS.” “Well,” said Mr. Hobbs, “he's pervided for between us, if he aint a earl.” “So he is,” said Dick. “I'd ha' stood by him. Blest if I didn't like that little feller fust-rate.” The very next morning, one of Dick's customers was rather surprised. He was a young lawyer just beginning practice--as poor as a very young lawyer can possibly be, but a bright, energetic young fellow, with sharp wit and a good temper. He had a shabby office near Dick's stand, and every morning Dick blacked his boots for him, and quite often they were not exactly water-tight, but he always had a friendly word or a joke for Dick.
